content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1.

The guidance: three steps: 1) sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). 2) Doebner modification to form the α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (alkene) from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid. 3) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine.

Thus retrosynthetic disconnections: target -> break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride) and an aniline (the phenyl with methyl). So precursor 1: p-toluidine (or 4-methyl aniline) with sulfonyl chloride attached to second phenyl ring? Actually target: p-tolyl attached to sulfonamide linking to second phenyl ring (sulfonyl attached to second phenyl). So disconnection: break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride attached to second phenyl (aryl sulfonyl chloride) and the aniline (p-toluidine). So precursor A: p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1). Precursor B: aryl sulfonyl chloride: c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2 attached to the rest? Wait the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the second phenyl which also bears the unsaturated amide side chain. So we need a phenyl sulfonyl chloride with a para substituent that is the unsaturated amide side chain (C=C-C(=O)N-Ph-NH2). Actually the target: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the sulfonyl group attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). The sulfonyl chloride precursor would be that phenyl ring bearing the side chain but with S(=O)(=O)Cl instead of NS(=O)(=O). So precursor B: c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2 with the side chain /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N attached at para position? Actually the side chain is attached to the phenyl ring at position para to sulfonyl? In SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the sulfonamide nitrogen attached to sulfonyl attached to phenyl (c2...). The phenyl has a para substituent /C=C/... So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2 with same para substituent. So we need to generate that via Doebner modification: the side chain is an α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid attached to phenyl via double bond, then amide formation with aniline (c3ccccc3N). So step 2: break amide to give carboxylic acid (α,β-unsaturated) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl ring via double bond: /C=C/C(=O)OH? Actually after breaking amide, we get α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid attached to phenyl: /C=C/C(=O)O (maybe). So precursor C: phenyl with para substituent α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2). This can be formed via Doebner modification from aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(/C=O)cc2) and malonic acid. So step 2: break double bond formation to give aldehyde and malonic acid. So precursor D: aromatic aldehyde (para-methyl? Actually the phenyl ring is unsubstituted except the para side chain). So aldehyde: c2ccc(C=O)cc2 (i.e., benzaldehyde). But also need the sulfonyl chloride later? Wait the phenyl ring also will later have sulfonyl chloride at para? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the same phenyl ring (the one bearing the side chain). So after step 2, we have phenyl with both aldehyde (or later unsaturated acid) and later sulfonyl chloride at same position? In target, sulfonyl attached at position 1 of phenyl, side chain at para (position 4). So the phenyl ring has two substituents: sulfonyl (connected to aniline) and the unsaturated amide side chain. In retrosynthesis, we can first form sulfonamide later, after we have sulfonyl chloride attached. So step 2 (Doebner) will produce the unsaturated acid on the phenyl ring that already has sulfonyl chloride? The sulfonyl chloride is attached to the phenyl ring; the Doebner modification would need the aromatic aldehyde bearing sulfonyl chloride substituent. So precursor for Doebner: aromatic aldehyde with sulfonyl chloride substituent (para). So we need to generate that aldehyde: c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)C=O? Actually the aldehyde at para to sulfonyl chloride. So the aldehyde is 4-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride. So step 2: break unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid. So precursor D: 4-formyl phenyl sulfonyl chloride (c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)C=O) (with methyl on other phenyl? Wait the other phenyl is the tolyl aniline). So final route:

Step 1 (retro): target -> sulfonamide disconnection -> precursors: p-toluidine (A) and sulfonyl chloride phenyl (B) which contains unsaturated amide side chain.

Step 2 (retro on B): break amide -> gives unsaturated acid phenyl (C) and aniline (c3ccccc3N) (the amine for amide). So B = sulfonyl chloride phenyl with unsaturated amide side chain. After breaking amide, we get sulfonyl chloride phenyl with α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (C) and aniline (E). So B = C + E via amide formation.

Step 3 (retro on C): break α,β-unsaturated acid to aldehyde (F) + malonic acid (common). So C = aldehyde phenyl sulfonyl chloride (F) + malonic acid (G) via Doebner.

Thus we have three steps.

Now we need to produce JSON route with nested reactions.

We need template IDs for each step. We have some templates from search results earlier. For amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine) we have template 401931 (retro: amide to acid + amine). That template seems to convert amide to acid + alkene? Actually its retro smarts: '[#7:2]-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:3])/[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5]>>C-C(-C)(-C)-O-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](-[#7:2])=[O;D1;H0:3].O-C(=O)-[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5]'. That's for amide with α,β-unsaturated acid? It splits into acid and amine plus a tert-butyl protecting group? Might be not ideal. But we can still use it.

For Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid) we need a template that breaks C-C double bond and forms aldehyde + malonic acid. Not sure we have one. Could search for functional_groups_broken: ["C-C double bonds"] and formed: ["aldehydes", "aliphatic carboxylic acid"] but earlier error due to carboxylic acid naming. Use "aliphatic carboxylic acid". Let's try search again.
